artifactStrategy.preservation: Store this content JSON sidecar next to the rendered Markdown PRD; implementation work items link to the rendered PRD.

contextGrounding.codebaseContext: Doc-Vader has a document-type-pack schema and metadata routing ADR, but runtime consumers still use repository-root artifact paths and no DocPackRegistry exists. Existing extension loading executes configured extension packages and must remain outside the registry boundary.
contextGrounding.adrAlignment: ADR-011 establishes metadata routing and format-adapter terminology. This PRD refines pack bundling and registry responsibilities without changing canonical route semantics.

problemStatement: Doc-Vader cannot package reusable documentation domains coherently because schemas, templates, contexts, profiles, and policy assets are rooted globally and many consumers hard-code their locations. A future pack mechanism must avoid conflating cataloging, sourcing, execution, business rules, and lifecycle management.
solution: Introduce domain-level doc-packs in gated phases. Define a doc-pack manifest distinct from document-type contributions, implement a catalog-only DocPackRegistry that registers and resolves opaque references, migrate sdlc-core as the pilot domain without compatibility shims, then migrate remaining domains independently with pack-owned tests and fixtures.

userStories.story: As a pack author, I want a domain bundle manifest distinct from a document-type contribution, so that a pack can own reusable artifacts and optional extension references without overloading routing metadata.

As a repository maintainer, I want DocPackRegistry to catalog only registered packs and opaque references, so that sourcing, activation, execution, lifecycle, and domain rules remain independently replaceable.
As a runtime host, I want extension declarations to be resolvable but not executed by the registry, so that explicit user consent and the third-party disclaimer stay at the activation seam.
As a pack consumer, I want logical artifact references instead of repository-root paths, so that a domain can move into a pack without compatibility aliases.

As an AFK implementation agent, I want each phase to have a committed scope, dependencies, prompts, tests, review lanes, and stop conditions, so that the next phase begins only after fresh evidence proves the prior phase.

coverageReview.notes: Stories cover authoring, catalog registration, executable-reference safety, consumer migration, and AFK delivery. Sourcing and lifecycle are intentionally excluded from the registry contract.

dimensions.name: grounding
dimensions.rationale: Grounded in current ADR, manifest, loader, and documented work items.

dimensions.name: coverage
dimensions.rationale: Covers all agreed registry boundaries and migration phases.

dimensions.name: decision-rationale
dimensions.rationale: Separates the deep registry catalog seam from variable sourcing and runtime hosting.

dimensions.name: testability
dimensions.rationale: Each phase has public seams and fail-closed command gates.

dimensions.name: automation-readiness
dimensions.rationale: Work is decomposed into dependency-ordered AFK tasks with structured handoffs.

qualityReview.notes: The PRD deliberately does not select a pack source or executable sandbox.

implementationDecisions.statement: Use a domain-level doc-pack manifest in addition to the existing document-type-pack contribution descriptor.
implementationDecisions.rationale: A domain bundle needs identity, dependencies, artifact collections, extension declarations, and test conventions that are not document-type routing concerns.

Registration identity, validation, authoritative listing, and opaque-reference resolution are cohesive; sourcing, loading, execution, hosting, business rules, and lifecycle would make the interface shallow and coupled.

implementationDecisions.statement: Do not implement a technical trust system in the MVP.
implementationDecisions.rationale: Third-party responsibility is communicated through a static disclaimer and explicit activation outside the registry. This avoids prematurely copying package-ecosystem concerns into one module.

implementationDecisions.statement: Use no legacy aliases or shims for internal migration.
implementationDecisions.rationale: External consumer compatibility is not required; direct logical references prevent a permanent compatibility layer and make extraction complete.

implementationDecisions.statement: Treat JSON-LD contexts as optional semantic-context artifacts.
implementationDecisions.rationale: Contexts provide syntax-agnostic interoperability where valuable, but every pack must define stable metadata semantics whether or not it publishes JSON-LD.

testingDecisions.behaviorContract: Registered packs can be validated and resolved by logical reference without source acquisition or runtime execution; each migrated pack proves its own metadata, body/content, renderer, and fixture behavior.

seams.name: Registry registration and resolution
seams.rationale: Tests must exercise the catalog boundary rather than its internal index.

seams.name: Manifest conformance
seams.rationale: Invalid identities, collisions, dependencies, and references must fail before registration.

seams.name: Pack-owned artifact behavior
seams.rationale: Each pack validates its metadata, content, renderer, semantic-context, and fixture contracts at its own boundary.

seams.name: Migrated command behavior
seams.rationale: Existing PRD, work-management, backlog, and task consumers must resolve logical references without legacy path fallbacks.

seamReview.notes: The registry and pack contracts are explicit public seams; runtime sourcing and execution are deliberately outside the scope.

outOfScope: Pack source adapters for disk, URL, package manager, or declarative discovery.
Runtime loading, execution, hosting, sandboxing, or lifecycle management of packs and extensions.
Hash, signature, provenance, attestation, expiry, or revocation trust systems.
External-consumer compatibility aliases for legacy repository-root paths.
A bulk migration of all domains in one changeset.
successCriteria: A committed Phase 1 inventory maps every built-in artifact and internal hard-coded path to a proposed logical artifact ID and domain owner.
DocPackRegistry has only registration identity, validation, authoritative list, and registered-reference resolution responsibilities.
sdlc-core migrates without legacy aliases and all affected commands pass focused and repository gates.
Every migrated pack owns its tests and fixtures.
Each AFK phase emits an acceptance report and the next phase starts only after a fresh clear validation gate.

handoffNotes: Use one worktree and one mutation-capable owner per phase.
Begin every phase from the accepted previous commit and re-check HEAD before its final gate.
Use TDD: add a failing focused test before each behavior change.
Run independent fresh-context, read-only architecture, scope, and test reviews after the writer handoff.
Stop instead of proceeding when a gate fails, a review finding is unresolved, the base commit is stale, or a product decision is needed.
The full phase prompts and commands are in the rendered PRD under AFK Execution Contract.

furtherNotes: Phase 4 domains are core, diataxis, agile, c4, rfx, dita, para, and operations when operational artifacts form a cohesive domain. Release notes belong to sdlc-core when they express delivery governance and to a product documentation domain when they are end-user communication; runbooks and playbooks belong to operations when that domain is introduced, otherwise sdlc-core provisionally.
